newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close 2.12 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: French shares close 2.12 percent higher.

text.p: French shares closed 2.12 percent higher on Tuesday in an upswing which was the latest in a series of wild movements on the heels of Wall Street. The rise was also underpinned by a firmer dollar.

Wall Street's early gains after a favourable March U.S. CPI figure extended Paris' early gains. Traders said the market's direction on Wednesday would be influenced by the March industrial production figure out that day.
The CAC-40 closed up 54.50 points, or 2.12 percent, at 2,620.63 while the April future contract was up 64 points at 2,727. Volume was 6.2 billion francs.
Software group Cap Gemini was the top gainer of the day, adding 8.66 percent to 364 francs.
LVMH was boosted by a big rise in 1997 first quarter results and added 4.66 percent to 1,347 francs. Christian Dior, which has a big stake in LVMH, posted a four percent gain to 846 francs.
SGS-Thomson made a 7.45 percent gain to 404 francs, recovering from Monday's share decline on the back of a drop in first quarter earnings.
State-controlled insurer GAN was the biggest lower with a 2.65 percent fall to 147 francs.
